results.text: Article 19 Specific rules on official controls and for action taken by the competent authorities in relation to the residues of relevant substances in food and feed 1. Official controls to verify compliance with the rules referred to in points (a) and (c) of Article 1(2) shall include official controls, to be performed at any stage of production, processing and distribution, on relevant substances including substances to be used in food contact materials, contaminants, non-authorised, prohibited and undesirable substances whose use or presence on crops or animals or to produce or process food or feed may result in residues of those substances in food or feed. 2. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 144 to supplement this Regulation by laying down rules for the performance of the official controls referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article and for action to be taken by the competent authorities following those official controls. results.regulation_title: REGULATION (EC) No 178/2002 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL
results.heading: Responsibilities
results.text: Article 17 Responsibilities 1. Food and feed business operators at all stages of production, processing and distribution within the businesses under their control shall ensure that foods or feeds satisfy the requirements of food law which are relevant to their activities and shall verify that such requirements are met. 2. Member States shall enforce food law, and monitor and verify that the relevant requirements of food law are fulfilled by food and feed business operators at all stages of production, processing and distribution. For that purpose, they shall maintain a system of official controls and other activities as appropriate to the circumstances, including public communication on food and feed safety and risk, food and feed safety surveillance and other monitoring activities covering all stages of production, processing and distribution. Member States shall also lay down the rules on measures and penalties applicable to infringements of food and feed law. The measures and penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

results.text: Article 49 Official controls at border control posts 1. To verify compliance with the applicable requirements laid down in the rules referred to in Article 1(2), the competent authorities shall perform official controls on the consignments of the categories of animals and goods referred to in Article 47(1) upon arrival of the consignment at the border control post. Those official controls shall include documentary checks, identity checks and physical checks. 2. Physical checks shall be performed where those checks concern: (a) animals, except aquatic animals, or meat and edible meat offal, by an official veterinarian, who may be assisted by staff trained in accordance with the requirements established under paragraph 5 in veterinary matters and designated by the competent authorities for that purpose; (b) aquatic animals, products of animal origin other than the ones referred to in point (a) of this paragraph, germinal products or animal by-products, by an official veterinarian or by staff trained in accordance with the requirements established under paragraph 5 and designated by the competent authorities for that purpose; (c) plants, plant products and other objects, by an official plant health officer. 3. The competent authorities at border control posts shall systematically perform official controls on consignments of animals being transported and on means of transport to verify compliance with the animal welfare requirements laid down in the rules referred to in Article 1(2). Competent authorities shall put in place arrangements to give priority to official controls on animals being transported and to reduce delays on such controls. 4. results.heading: Food safety requirements
results.text: Article 14 Food safety requirements 1. Food shall not be placed on the market if it is unsafe. 2. Food shall be deemed to be unsafe if it is considered to be: (a) injurious to health; (b) unfit for human consumption. 3. In determining whether any food is unsafe, regard shall be had: (a) to the normal conditions of use of the food by the consumer and at each stage of production, processing and distribution, and (b) to the information provided to the consumer, including information on the label, or other information generally available to the consumer concerning the avoidance of specific adverse health effects from a particular food or category of foods. 4. In determining whether any food is injurious to health, regard shall be had: (a) not only to the probable immediate and/or short-term and/or long-term effects of that food on the health of a person consuming it, but also on subsequent generations; (b) to the probable cumulative toxic effects; (c) to the particular health sensitivities of a specific category of consumers where the food is intended for that category of consumers. 5. In determining whether any food is unfit for human consumption, regard shall be had to whether the food is unacceptable for human consumption according to its intended use, for reasons of contamination, whether by extraneous matter or otherwise, or through putrefaction, deterioration or decay. 6. ## 1. Short answer

The fact that aflatoxin B1 was detected does **not by itself establish that the figs are non-compliant**: the concentration and the applicable product classification are not stated. For dried figs, Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, Table 1, row 1.1.3 sets a maximum level of **6.0 μg/kg for aflatoxin B1** and **10.0 μg/kg for the sum of aflatoxins**. Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Article 2, prohibits placing food covered by the Annex on the market when it exceeds the applicable maximum level.

The import-control rules are a separate issue. The frozen-corpus entry for dried figs from Türkiye is in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Annex II, Section 1, row 14, with a **30% identity and physical check frequency**. That entry also entails consignment documentation requirements under Articles 10 and 11. Whether the shipment falls within that entry depends on its product/CN classification.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Contaminant limit:** Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, Table 1, row **1.1.3** (“Dried figs”) gives the aflatoxin B1 and total-aflatoxin levels above. The row’s remark extends those levels to food consisting of dried figs as its only ingredient and to processed products consisting of at least 80% dried figs; for other products, Article 3(1) and (2) govern. The classification and any processing or ingredient composition therefore matter. The general market prohibition is in Article 2.
- **Import controls:** Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Article 7 and Annex II, Section 1, row **14**, cover the listed Türkiye dried-fig products by the specified CN/TARIC classifications. Article 8 provides for identity and physical checks, including sampling and laboratory analysis, at the frequency stated in Annex II. The corpus entry reports 30% for the dried-fig row; that is a control frequency, not a finding about this particular consignment.
- **Accompanying documents:** For Annex II consignments, Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Article 10 requires results of sampling and analyses performed by the relevant third-country competent authority; Article 11 requires an official certificate. Article 4 requires a duly finalised CHED before release for free circulation. These requirements depend on the consignment being within the relevant Annex II product classification.
- **Responsible actors and possible action:** Under Regulation (EC) No 178/2002, Article 17, food business operators must ensure compliance within their activities. Article 14 prohibits placing unsafe food on the market. If an operator has reason to believe food already placed on the market is not compliant with food-safety requirements, Article 19 sets out withdrawal, notification and, where necessary, consumer-recall duties. For official enforcement, Regulation (EU) 2017/625, Articles 65 and 138, address suspected and established non-compliance respectively; the measures taken depend on the competent authority’s findings.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

The stated facts do not give the measured B1 concentration, the total-aflatoxin result, the analytical basis, the precise CN/TARIC classification, or whether the figs are sold as dried figs or incorporated into a processed product. Without those facts, neither a violation of the maximum level nor the precise import-control treatment can be concluded.

Cellar metadata checks observed consolidations dated **2026-08-19** for Regulation 2023/915, **2026-06-30** for Regulation 2019/1793, **2026-01-01** for Regulation 178/2002, and **2025-01-05** for Regulation 2017/625. These are metadata observations, not verification that each cited provision is currently effective as applicable to this shipment. Before relying on them, check amendments, entry into force and application dates, transitional rules, Annex changes, and product-specific classification.
